description: Studio recipes: structured starting points for analyst work. Each recipe is a chain of frames (so Present can walk through them) holding prompt cards. Templates only: not expert-certified answers, and nothing here fetches outside data.

recipes.title: Issue Tree
recipes.summary: One key question, MECE branches, a hypothesis for each, and the analyses that would prove or kill it.
recipes.guide: Hypothesis-driven issue tree: start from one key question, split it into mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive branches, state a hypothesis for each, then list the analysis that would test it. A standard consulting structure offered as a template, not an expert-checked answer.

cards.title: Key question
cards.summary: One sentence: what decision, for whom, by when? Example: should we enter this market?

cards.title: Branch A
cards.summary: Name one driver of the answer.

cards.title: Branch B
cards.summary: A second driver, with no overlap with A.

cards.title: Branch C
cards.summary: A third driver, so nothing important is missing.

cards.title: MECE check
cards.summary: No overlap between branches. Nothing important missing.

cards.title: Hypothesis for A
cards.summary: If this is true, what would we see in the data?

cards.title: Hypothesis for B
cards.summary: If this is true, what would we see in the data?

cards.title: Hypothesis for C
cards.summary: If this is true, what would we see in the data?

cards.title: Analysis for A
cards.summary: Data needed · method · due

cards.title: Analysis for B
cards.summary: Data needed · method · due

cards.title: Analysis for C
cards.summary: Data needed · method · due

recipes.title: Deal Thesis
recipes.summary: A thesis, the few value drivers behind it, what could break it, the diligence that tests it, and when you would walk away.
recipes.guide: A one-page deal logic for a PE case: a thesis, the value drivers behind it, the risks that could break it, the diligence questions that test them and the conditions under which you would walk away. A template to structure thinking, not an investment recommendation.

cards.title: Thesis
cards.summary: Why this business, at this price, with this plan? One paragraph.

cards.title: Driver 1
cards.summary: Example prompt: revenue growth. What has to be true?

cards.title: Driver 2
cards.summary: Example prompt: margin. What has to be true?

cards.title: Driver 3
cards.summary: Example prompt: cash conversion. What has to be true?

cards.title: Risk 1
cards.summary: What would break the thesis?

cards.title: Risk 2
cards.summary: What would break the thesis?

cards.title: Risk 3
cards.summary: What would break the thesis?

cards.title: Question 1
cards.summary: Which risk does it test? What evidence settles it?

cards.title: Question 2
cards.summary: Which risk does it test? What evidence settles it?

cards.title: Question 3
cards.summary: Which risk does it test? What evidence settles it?

cards.title: Walk-away condition 1
cards.summary: If this is true, we do not proceed.

cards.title: Walk-away condition 2
cards.summary: Price, structure or evidence that ends the deal.

recipes.title: IC Memo Spine
recipes.summary: Eight sections of an investment-committee memo, so you fill the structure from evidence rather than from the pitch deck.
recipes.guide: An investment-committee memo spine for an early-stage deal. Each frame is one section; fill it from evidence, not from the pitch deck. A structure to rehearse, not a finished memo. A template to fill in, not an answer key.

cards.title: Recommendation
cards.summary: Invest, pass or wait, with the single strongest reason.

cards.title: Market size and timing
cards.summary: Bottom-up if you can. Why now?

cards.title: Product and edge
cards.summary: What do customers do differently because of it?

cards.title: Traction
cards.summary: Cohorts, retention, net revenue retention. Evidence, not claims.

cards.title: Team and gaps
cards.summary: What is proven, what is missing, who fills it?

cards.title: Round terms
cards.summary: Price, instrument, preferences.

cards.title: Ownership after dilution
cards.summary: Ownership now and after the next round.

cards.title: Risk 1
cards.summary: What would make this a loss?

cards.title: Risk 2
cards.summary: What would make this a loss?

cards.title: Ask and conditions
cards.summary: What do you want the committee to approve, and on what conditions?

recipes.title: Story Bank
recipes.summary: Six behavioural stories in STAR form, one per common competency.
recipes.guide: Six behavioural stories in STAR form (Situation, Task, Action, Result). Put a number in the Result only if you honestly have one; never invent an outcome. A template for practice, not a script.

cards.title: Failure story
cards.summary:
S: …
T: …
A: …
R and what you changed: …

recipes.title: Company Map
recipes.summary: One page for a target firm: what it does, the people you are approaching, the roles you target, and what you still need to learn.
recipes.guide: A one-page map of a target firm: what it does, the people you are approaching, the roles you are targeting and what you still need to learn. Names come from your own Outreach board; nothing is looked up online. A template to fill in, not an answer key.

cards.title: What they do
cards.summary: In your own words, after reading their site.

cards.title: Why this firm
cards.summary: One specific reason, not a compliment.

cards.title: Person 1
cards.summary: Role · stage · last touch

cards.title: Role to apply for
cards.summary: Deadline · CV version · status

cards.title: Question 1
cards.summary: What do I still need to know?

cards.title: Question 2
cards.summary: What do I still need to know?

cards.title: Research notes
cards.summary: Recent news, with the source and date.

recipes.title: Weekly Map
recipes.summary: A weekly review in four boxes: this week's three, wins, carry-over, and what to learn next.
recipes.guide: A weekly review in four boxes. Close what you can, carry over only what you must, and choose next week's three. A template to fill in, not an answer key.
